findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. This alone answers "what is it" and "why does it matter".
findings.source: header, first lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The second section shows an error, and the reader meets it before any content. The lede promises that Athena records models, verdict and cost, and this section was meant to show that, but it shows nothing. A newcomer is likely to read this as a broken site.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This is Athena's home page, but the title and almost all of the body are about a different project, firstmate. The third lede explains that the page is a sample study. Even so, a newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to scroll past a long, dense study of another tool before reaching Athena's own install steps.
findings.source: title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The next step is easy to find. A link at the top jumps to concrete steps: clone the repo, check the prerequisites, run setup.sh, then try one example command. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and Next steps: "Install Athena from the checkout: ./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The page does not say which repository the command acts on (probably the current directory). It also does not mention that Claude Code needs an account or a paid plan. A first-time user may hit either of these gaps.
findings.source: Next steps: "press Enter to run it on your repository"

findings.text: This link is aimed at the site owner but sits in the newcomer's opening header. It is not clear who "your" refers to, which may confuse a first-time visitor.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Several glossary entries say only that the term is undefined. This is honest and fits the traced-claims approach. Still, a newcomer who looks up these terms learns little.
findings.source: Glossary entries for captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake: "The firstmate source does not define ..."

findings.text: The study shows its method clearly: every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to specific file lines at a pinned commit. This works as a demonstration of what Athena produces. The section on firstmate itself is in plain language and defines its terms before using them.
findings.source: Start here / States / Transitions / Claims and sources (c1–c45 with line-level links)
